test_name: Search for a Connector and Verify Results
description: This test verifies that the user can search for a specific connector using the search functionality and the results are displayed accurately.
steps: Type 'Postgres' into the search input field.
Press the 'Enter' key to submit the search query.
Verify that the connectors list updates to show only connectors matching 'Postgres'.
Click on the first connector in the filtered list to view its details.
Verify that the connector details page displays information relevant to 'Postgres'.
expected_results: Only connectors matching the search query 'Postgres' are displayed.
Clicking on a connector navigates to its details page with accurate information.
edge_cases: Search with an empty query should return all connectors.
Search with a query that has no matches should display a 'No Results' message.
Search with special characters should not cause errors.
Search with a very long string should not break the UI.
Search with partial matches should return connectors containing the query string.
data_requirements: A connector named 'Postgres' exists in the system.
The connectors list contains at least 10 entries.
Connectors have unique names for verification.
A test user with access to the 'Connectors' page is available.
The search functionality is configured and operational.
dependencies: User is logged in and has access to the 'Connectors' tab.
Test environment has sufficient connectors for validation.
Search indexing is correctly set up for connectors.
api_interactions: Fetch connectors API call triggered by the search query.
Verify the response payload for accuracy.
performance_metrics: Search results should load within 2 seconds.
Page responsiveness should not degrade after multiple searches.
accessibility_requirements: Search input field should be accessible via keyboard.
Search button (if any) should have an ARIA label.
Results should be readable by screen readers.
